title: Heterogeneous circuit-breaker thresholds led to cascading SLO misses during dual-region failover
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: On 2026-02-18 at ~03:07 UTC, an auto-scaling event in primary region us-west-2 caused a sustained degradation of instance availability. The control plane routed a percentage of traffic to eu-west-1 as part of our failover policy. Because circuit-breaker (CB) thresholds and hysteresis settings differed between regions, the secondary region accepted higher instantaneous load while the primary region was still partially degraded. That mismatch amplified KV cache warmup and increased per-request CPU/GPU memory pressure in eu-west-1, which caused progressive latency tail increases and triggered additional circuit-breakers and aggressive load-shedding. The net result was a sustained SLO miss for 37 minutes across chat and generation routes affecting ~14% of production requests. This postmortem captures timeline, root cause, immediate mitigations, and tracked follow-up action items.
timeline: 2026-02-18 03:06 UTC - Scheduled autoscaler churn in us-west-2 removed ~22% of available serving capacity due to a mis-sized scaling policy during a minor load spike.
2026-02-18 03:07 UTC - Control plane detected degraded capacity in us-west-2 and initiated traffic migration to eu-west-1 per routing policy.
2026-02-18 03:09 UTC - eu-west-1 observed a sudden 2.5x qps burst for generation endpoints; local circuit-breakers began tripping on concurrent_request_thresholds configured higher than us-west-2.

2026-02-18 03:12 UTC - KV cache miss-rate in eu-west-1 rose from 4% to 42% as new requests warmed cold caches; per-token latency increased, causing additional cascading CB trips and load-shedding of lower-priority requests.
2026-02-18 03:20 UTC - Pager duty engaged; SRE team enacted emergency traffic dampening and temporarily reduced global routing weight to eu-west-1.
2026-02-18 03:35 UTC - Capacity autoscaler in us-west-2 recovered incrementally; control plane slowly rebalanced traffic back with staged rollbacks.
2026-02-18 03:43 UTC - All routes within SLO; incident declared resolved at 03:47 UTC after monitoring confirmed stable tail latency.
2026-02-18 04:15 UTC - Initial incident report filed; mitigation steps documented; follow-up triage scheduled.
2026-02-19 - Postmortem draft completed and reviewed by on-call SRE and runtime owners.
2026-02-25 - Final postmortem reviewed and marked done after follow-up items assigned and scheduled.
Notes: timestamps are rounded to minute-level; detailed logs and traces are attached in links below.
impact_summary: Duration: 37 minutes of sustained SLO degradation. Customer-facing impact: ~14% of production requests experienced elevated tail latency > 99th percentile and increased error rates due to load-shedding on lower-priority routes. Internal metrics: request success rate dropped from 99.6% to 85.3% at peak for affected routes. No data exfiltration or security breach.
detection_and_response: Detection: Platform alerting fired on composite SLO threshold (tail-latency > 99th percentile). Response: on-call SRE investigated routing and found region-weight shift; temporarily reduced eu-west-1 weight and applied emergency damping. The runtime team adjusted per-region CB counters to prevent repeated immediate re-openings. We used Grafana dashboards (runtime-tail-latency) and request traces to validate that mitigation reduced tail latency.
root_cause: Primary root cause was inconsistent circuit-breaker and load-shedding configuration between regions combined with an aggressive autoscaler policy in us-west-2. Specific contributors: 1) CB concurrent_request_threshold was 20% higher in eu-west-1 than in us-west-2, enabling a higher instantaneous acceptance of requests that the secondary region's cache and memory bandwidth could not sustain. 2) Load-shedding priorities were not region-aware; when eu-west-1 began shedding, it dropped lower-priority but high-error-reduction requests, which increased pressure on other internal subsystems. 3) Autoscaler in us-west-2 used a reactive policy that aggressively removed instances during brief CPU spikes, exposing the system to loss of warm capacity. 4) Monitoring lacked a cross-region composite alert that would have considered imbalance signals and prevented gradual amplification.
mitigations: Emergency: reduced eu-west-1 routing weight by 60% until caches warmed and we validated tail latency improved.
Emergency: temporarily relaxed CB hysteresis so tripped breakers did not immediately re-open and re-trip, preventing oscillation.
Emergency: increased short-term reserve capacity in us-west-2 (manual bump) until autoscaler tuning is complete.
Operational: added synthetic canary traffic across regions to exercise failover paths and warm caches continuously.
Operational: updated incident runbook to include cross-region CB mismatch checks and an explicit step to inspect cache warmup metrics.
Monitoring: created a composite alert rule that triggers when primary region capacity drops and secondary region qps increases by >1.5x within 5 minutes.
Documentation: added a configuration checklist for region parity that enumerates all CB and load-shedding parameters that must be equalized or documented with a reasoned deviation.
followups: F1: Unify circuit-breaker baseline and hysteresis across regions unless explicitly scoped. Owner: Priya Raman. Due: 2026-03-12. Issue: ENG-24179
F2: Rework autoscaler policy to use predictive smoothing and minimum warm pool for serving nodes to avoid removing hot capacity on short spikes. Owner: Daniel Cho. Due: 2026-04-01. Issue: ENG-24205
F3: Implement region-aware load-shedding priorities so that critical request classes are preserved during cross-region failovers. Owner: Marcus Lee. Due: 2026-03-22. Issue: ENG-24198
F4: Add cross-region synthetic canaries and a dashboard showing inter-region qps ratios, cache-miss deltas, and CB open rate. Owner: SRE team (on-call rotation). Due: 2026-03-05. Issue: ENG-24162

F5: Create automated parity tests in CI that assert critical runtime configs (CB thresholds, hysteresis, load-shedding tiers) are within allowed variance across regions. Owner: CI Platform. Due: 2026-03-19. Issue: ENG-24222

F6: Expand SLO alerting to include composite signals (cross-region qps imbalance + tail latency) and add a playbook to throttle global traffic before switching region weights. Owner: Monitoring team. Due: 2026-03-12. Issue: ENG-24201
F7: Postmortem review and sign-off with Product and Support; public incident summary for customers impacted. Owner: Ava Martinez. Due: 2026-03-01. Issue: PM-410
